docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: This section provides detailed documentation for all available API endpoints.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: https://api.example.com

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require authentication using an API key. Include your API key in the request header:

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

docs.title: GET /api/v1/resources
docs.text:
Retrieve a list of resources.

Parameters:

Name Type Required Description page integer No Page number for pagination limit integer No Number of items per page

Response:

{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "description": "string"
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "total": "integer",
    "page": "integer",
    "limit": "integer"
  }
}

docs.title: POST /api/v1/resources
docs.text:
Create a new resource.

Request Body:

{
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string"
}

Response:

{
  "id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "description": "string"
}

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text: All endpoints may return the following error responses:

docs.title: 400 Bad Request
docs.text:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "string",
    "message": "string",
    "details": {}
  }
}

docs.title: 401 Unauthorized
docs.text:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "Invalid or missing API key"
  }
}

docs.title: 404 Not Found
docs.text:
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "Resource not found"
  }
}

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
API requests are limited to: - 100 requests per minute per API key - 1000 requests per hour per API key

Rate limit headers are included in all responses:

X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 95
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1612345678

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: List endpoints support pagination using the following parameters: - page: The page number (1-based) - limit: Number of items per page (default: 20, max: 100)

docs.title: Versioning
docs.text: The API is versioned through the URL path. The current version is v1.

docs.title: Authentication Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to authenticate your API requests.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: API keys are the primary method of authentication for our API. Each API key is associated with a specific account and has its own set of permissions.

docs.title: Obtaining an API Key
docs.text:
1. Log in to your account
  2. Navigate to the API Keys section
  3. Click "Create New API Key"
  4. Select the required permissions
  5. Copy the generated API key

docs.title: Using Your API Key
docs.text:
Include your API key in the request header:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" https://api.example.com/v1/resources

docs.title: Java
docs.text:
ApiClient client = new ApiClient();
client.setApiKey("YOUR_API_KEY");

docs.title: Python
docs.text:
config = Configuration(api_key={"Authorization": "YOUR_API_KEY"})
client = ApiClient(config)

docs.title: TypeScript
docs.text:
const config = new Configuration({
    apiKey: "YOUR_API_KEY"
});

  7. Generate new keys
  8. Revoke old keys

  9. Update your applications

  10. Monitor key usage

  12. Set up alerts for unusual activity
  13. Review permissions regularly

docs.title: Coding Standards
docs.text:
1. Python 

    # Use type hints
def process_item(item: Dict[str, Any]) -> Result:
    """
    Process an item and return the result.

    Args:
        item: The item to process

    Returns:
        Result object with processed data
    """
    return Result(item["id"], process_data(item))

  2. Java 

    // Use proper JavaDoc
/**
 * Processes an item and returns the result.
 *
 * @param item The item to process
 * @return Result object with processed data
 * @throws InvalidItemException if item is invalid
 */
public Result processItem(Item item) {
    validateItem(item);
    return new Result(item.getId(), processData(item));
}

  3. TypeScript 

    // Use interfaces and types
interface Item {
  id: string;
  data: Record<string, unknown>;
}

function processItem(item: Item): Result {
  validateItem(item);
  return new Result(item.id, processData(item));
}

docs.text: This guide provides practical examples of using our API with different programming languages and use cases.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
# Python
from api_client import ApiClient

client = ApiClient()
client.configure_auth("YOUR_API_KEY")

// Java
import com.example.client.ApiClient;

ApiClient client = new ApiClient();
client.setApiKey("YOUR_API_KEY");

// TypeScript

const client = new ApiClient({

});

docs.title: Making API Calls
docs.text:
# Python
response = client.resources.list()
for item in response.data:
    print(f"ID: {item.id}, Name: {item.name}")

// Java
ResourceResponse response = client.resources().list();
response.getData().forEach(item -> {
    System.out.printf("ID: %s, Name: %s%n", item.getId(), item.getName());
});

// TypeScript
const response = await client.resources.list();
response.data.forEach(item => {
  console.log(`ID: ${item.id}, Name: ${item.name}`);
});

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
# Python
page = 1
while True:
    response = client.resources.list(page=page, limit=100)
    if not response.data:
        break
    for item in response.data:
        process_item(item)
    page += 1

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
# Python
from time import sleep
from api_client.exceptions import RateLimitError

def make_request_with_retry(func, max_retries=3):
    for attempt in range(max_retries):
        try:
            return func()
        except RateLimitError as e:
            if attempt == max_retries - 1:
                raise
            sleep(e.retry_after)

# Python
def batch_process(items, batch_size=100):
    for i in range(0, len(items), batch_size):
        batch = items[i:i + batch_size]
        client.resources.batch_create(batch)

# Python
import unittest
from unittest.mock import Mock

class TestApiClient(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.client = ApiClient()

    def test_list_resources(self):

# Python
import os
import unittest

class TestApiIntegration(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.client = ApiClient()
        self.client.configure_auth(os.getenv('API_KEY'))

    def test_create_and_delete_resource(self):

            'name': 'Test Resource'

        self.assertIsNotNone(resource['id'])

docs.title: What is this API?
docs.text: Our API provides a comprehensive set of endpoints for managing and accessing resources in your applications. It follows REST principles and uses standard HTTP methods for operations.

docs.title: Which programming languages are supported?
docs.text:
We provide official SDKs for: - Python - Java - TypeScript/JavaScript - Go - Ruby

However, you can use any language that can make HTTP requests to interact with our API.

docs.title: How do I get started?
docs.text:
1. Sign up for an account at example.com/signup
  2. Get your API key from the dashboard
  3. Follow our Getting Started Guide
  4. Check out our code examples

docs.title: How do I authenticate my requests?
docs.text:
Use your API key in the Authorization header: 

Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

docs.title: Where do I find my API key?
docs.text: You can find your API key in your account dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

docs.title: Can I regenerate my API key?
docs.text: Yes, you can regenerate your API key from the dashboard. Remember to update all your applications with the new key.

docs.title: How do I handle API key rotation?
docs.text: We recommend: 1. Generate a new API key 2. Update your applications to use the new key 3. Monitor for any calls using the old key 4. Delete the old key once all systems are updated

docs.title: What are the rate limits?
docs.text:
• Free tier: 1,000 requests per hour
  • Pro tier: 10,000 requests per hour
  • Enterprise tier: Custom limits

docs.title: How do I handle rate limiting?
docs.text:
1. Check the X-RateLimit-* headers in responses
  2. Implement exponential backoff
  3. Consider upgrading your plan if you consistently hit limits

docs.title: What happens when I exceed the rate limit?
docs.text: You'll receive a 429 Too Many Requests response. The Retry-After header indicates when you can resume making requests.

docs.title: How is my data protected?
docs.text:
• All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3
  • Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256
  • Regular security audits and penetration testing
  • SOC 2 Type II certified

docs.title: Do you store sensitive data?
docs.text: We follow data minimization principles and only store what's necessary for API operations. See our security documentation for details.

docs.title: How long do you retain data?
docs.text:
• Active data: Retained while your account is active
  • Deleted data: Removed within 30 days
  • Logs: Retained for 90 days

docs.title: What does each error code mean?
docs.text:
• 400: Bad Request - Check your request parameters
  • 401: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing API key
  • 403: Forbidden - Valid API key but insufficient permissions
  • 404: Not Found - Resource doesn't exist
  • 429: Too Many Requests - Rate limit exceeded
  • 500: Internal Server Error - Contact support

docs.title: How should I handle errors?
docs.text:
1. Always check the response status code
  2. Read the error message in the response body
  3. Implement appropriate retry logic
  4. Log errors for debugging

docs.title: How is billing calculated?
docs.text:
• Based on API calls per month
  • Additional charges for specific features
  • Billed monthly or annually
  • Volume discounts available

docs.title: Can I change my plan?
docs.text: Yes, you can upgrade or downgrade your plan at any time from the dashboard. Changes take effect immediately.

docs.title: How do I cancel my account?
docs.text:
1. Contact support to initiate cancellation
  2. Export any necessary data
  3. Delete your API keys
  4. Confirm cancellation

1. Documentation
  2. Community Forums
  3. Stack Overflow
  4. Email support (premium plans)

docs.title: How do I report bugs?
docs.text: See our bug reporting guidelines for instructions on submitting issues.

docs.title: Can I request new features?
docs.text: Yes! Submit feature requests through: 1. GitHub Issues 2. Community Forums 3. Direct contact (enterprise customers)

docs.title: How can I optimize my API usage?
docs.text:
1. Use pagination for large datasets
  2. Implement caching where appropriate
  3. Batch operations when possible
  4. Monitor your usage patterns

1. Not handling rate limits properly
  2. Ignoring error responses
  3. Hard-coding API keys
  4. Missing retry logic
  5. Insufficient error logging

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: This guide provides detailed instructions for migrating between API versions. Each section covers the changes required and best practices for a smooth transition.

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
1. Authentication Changes 
    - Authorization: ApiKey YOUR_API_KEY
+ Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN
  2. Migrate from API key to OAuth 2.0
  3. Update token management

  4. Implement refresh token flow

  5. Response Format Updates 

    // Old format
{
  "status": "success",
  "data": { ... }
}

// New format
{
  "data": { ... },
  "meta": {
    "requestId": "abc123",
    "timestamp": "2024-03-15T12:00:00Z"
  }
}

  6. Endpoint Changes

  7. /v1/* endpoints removed
  8. New endpoints under /v2/*
  9. Updated parameter names and types

docs.title: Migration Steps
docs.text:
1. Pre-Migration Checklist
  2. Audit current API usage
  3. Document custom integrations
  4. Back up critical data

  5. Review deprecation notices

  6. Authentication Updates 

    # Old authentication
client.api_key = "your-api-key"

# New authentication
client.configure_oauth({
  "client_id": "your-client-id",
  "client_secret": "your-client-secret"
})

  7. Response Handling 

    # Old way
if response.status == "success":
    data = response.data

# New way
data = response.data
request_id = response.meta.request_id

  8. SDK Updates 

    # Update SDK version
pip install --upgrade example-api-client>=2.0.0

  9. Testing Process

  10. Test in development environment
  11. Validate all API calls
  12. Check error handling
  13. Monitor performance

response = client.create_resource({
  "name": "Example",
  "type": "test"

# v2.x
response = client.resources.create({
  "name": "Example",
  "type": "test",
  "metadata": {
    "version": "2.0"
  }
})

  2. Error Handling 

    # v1.x
try:
  response = client.get_resource(id)
  if response.status == "error":
    handle_error(response.error)
except ApiException as e:
  handle_exception(e)

# v2.x
try:
  resource = client.resources.get(id)
except ResourceNotFound as e:
  handle_not_found(e)
except ApiError as e:
  handle_api_error(e)

docs.title: Available SDKs
docs.text: Our API is available through multiple SDKs, making it easy to integrate with your preferred programming language.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Add the dependency to your pom.xml:

<dependency>
    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>api-client</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0</version>
</dependency>

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
import com.example.client.ApiClient;
import com.example.client.api.DefaultApi;

ApiClient client = new ApiClient();
client.setBasePath("https://api.example.com");

DefaultApi api = new DefaultApi(client);
// Use the API methods
